sample_unit: observations (physician ratings across 6 dimensions of AI responses to hypothetical case vignettes; 37 physicians)

links.outcome: Physician-rated evidence quality of retrieval-augmented context-specific AI versus general-purpose AI
links.effect: Evidence quality VITA 4.46 vs ChatGPT 3.14 (42% relative gap); composite 25.4 vs 22.3 (+3.1, t = 8.31, p < 0.001). Retrieval augmentation was bundled with local context, so its effect is not isolated.
links.quote: The largest advantage was in evidence quality (VITA: 4.46 vs. ChatGPT: 3.14, a 42% relative gap).

unlisted_practices: Tailoring clinical AI assistants to local guidelines, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and formulary constraints in LMIC settings

screen.reason: Prospective multi-site evaluation by physicians using clinical case vignettes comparing a general-purpose LLM to a context-specific retrieval-augmented clinical reasoning tool adapted with local guidelines and formulary constraints.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented grounding with local guidelines and constraints
